macrostructure: site-wide: 'Book a call' primary CTA gets a signature hover
brief: Sibt-e-Ali portfolio — user clarified the previous CTA-interactivity sweep should have focused specifically on the 'Book a call' button (.nav-cta in the sticky nav on all 13 pages, .btn--primary on the hero/contact-page/closing-CTA), not every button site-wide. Since it's the actual conversion CTA, gave it more than the plain press-scale every other button already has: hover now lifts translateY(-2px) and adds an accent-tinted glow. Used filter:drop-shadow instead of box-shadow deliberately -- both .btn and .nav-cta already set overflow:hidden to clip their ink-wipe-fill ::before pseudo-element, which would also silently clip a box-shadow glow at the pill's edge (would have shipped invisible); filter composites after the element's own clipping so it isn't cut off. :active combines the lift with the existing scale(0.97) press rather than snapping back down and losing the lift mid-click. Removed a duplicate/now-stale .nav-cta:active rule that the new combined one superseded. .btn--secondary and every other CTA on the site (Source Code buttons, case-study CTAs, etc.) intentionally keep the plain press-scale from the earlier sweep -- this richer treatment is reserved for the one button whose entire job is to be noticed.

Sibt-e-Ali portfolio — user asked to make CTA buttons interactive site-wide via find-animation-opportunities. Swept every button-shaped CTA class across index.css, projects.css, and all 9 case-study <style> blocks against the gate: frequency=occasional (clicked a few times per session), purpose=Feedback (confirm the press registered), speed=140ms scale matching .btn:active's existing convention exactly (extending an approved pattern, not inventing a new one) -- passed cleanly. Found the pattern had NOT traveled everywhere .btn's CTA voice got reimplemented: .project-featured__source-link/.project-featured__primary-link/.project-supporting__source-link/.project-supporting__primary-link (projects.css) had hover only, no :active. Bigger find: two case-study pages (zen.html, go-blueprint.html) use their own CTA class (.zen-cta__link, .gob-cta__link respectively) instead of .cs-cta__link -- they were invisible to the earlier 7-page .cs-cta__link batch fix, so they STILL had both the missing :active state AND the border-radius:var(--radius-card) pill-button bug that was fixed everywhere else weeks ago. Fixed both classes the same way (radius-pill + :active scale). Deliberately left .proj__link/.project-featured__link/.channel-card__link/.video-card__link/.content-section__link alone -- these are text-with-arrow links, not button-shaped chips, and a press-scale on inline text reads oddly compared to a bordered/filled pill; that's a different, already-correct affordance tier, not a gap.

Sibt-e-Ali portfolio — user asked to make the video cards feel lively/interactive, floated the idea of playing a bit of the video on hover, asked to gate it through find-animation-opportunities. Gate: occasional frequency (browsing once), purpose named as explanation/delight (YouTube's own homepage does the same pattern), speed and function fine as long as it's built carefully -- the two real risks are wasted network requests from a passing cursor and orphaned playback/loads after mouseleave. Implemented in nav.js: a genuine 450ms hover-intent delay before lazily creating a muted (mute=1), controls-free (controls=0) YouTube iframe embed absolutely positioned over the static thumbnail (fades in via a .is-playing class + CSS opacity transition, avoiding a flash of empty iframe while it loads); mouseleave removes the iframe from the DOM entirely rather than just hiding it, so nothing keeps playing or downloading off-screen. Skipped outright (not degraded) for touch devices ((hover: hover) and (pointer: fine) check) and prefers-reduced-motion, since autoplaying video is exactly what that preference exists to suppress -- no 'gentler' version made sense here. .video-card__preview has pointer-events:none so clicks still pass through to the real <a> link underneath rather than hitting the embed's own surface. Added .video-card__preview to index.css's reduced-motion transition-none list.

macrostructure: Showcase + Letter (video-card row layout fix + article-link affordance)
brief: Sibt-e-Ali portfolio — two asks. (1) User said forcing 3 video cards per row cropped the thumbnails and didn't read as real cards ('static content as before'); wanted 1 per row like YouTube's own list view. Rebuilt .video-grid as a flex column (was CSS grid, 3-col) and .video-card as a horizontal row (thumbnail ~320px/42% left, title+desc+watch-link right), with real card chrome (bg/radius/shadow/hover-lift) matching .proj/.stack-card. Caught a real bug in the process: the thumbnail was forced to aspect-ratio:16/9 with object-fit:cover, but YouTube's hqdefault.jpg is natively 4:3 -- that combination was cropping real thumbnail content off the top/bottom. Fixed to aspect-ratio:4/3 (hqdefault's real ratio) so the full thumbnail shows uncropped, per the user's explicit ask. Stacks to thumbnail-on-top under 768px. (2) User asked (via find-animation-opportunities + hallmark) to make article-title links more visually distinct since they currently read as plain text. Gate: occasional frequency (scan once), purpose = state-indication (legibility fix, not decoration), 150-200ms, transform/color only -- passed. Added a leading '>' chevron (mono, --color-accent-dim, always visible so the affordance is legible before hover too) plus an underline that draws in via scaleX(0->1) and nudges the chevron translateX(2px) on hover, to .channel-card__posts a (Substack/Medium/YouTube lists on contact.html).

Built a new .content-section between About and the closing Contact CTA: 3 .video-card items (real thumbnail in a plain rounded frame + hover play-icon overlay -- a content affordance, not re-drawn player chrome), a footer linking to the full playlist and to Instagram (link-only, same no-scrapable-content reasoning as the contact.html Instagram card). Fetching the video data was non-trivial: YouTube's /@acodingmaniac/playlists page HTML embeds playlist metadata as lockupViewModel JSON (found the System Design playlist there, list=PLBXsGWRvtpFE, 8 videos), then the playlist's own page embeds each video's real title the same way -- paired 8 video IDs positionally with 8 titles (order matched playlist display order). No RSS equivalent exists for a single YouTube playlist the way Medium/Substack have feeds. Added a YouTube card (3 real video titles + links + 'watch full playlist' link) and an Instagram card (link-only -- Instagram's profile HTML is behind an auth wall with no reliably scrapable real post data, so no reel titles were fabricated or guessed). macrostructure: site-wide: animation-opportunity fixes + mobile nav bug fix
brief: Sibt-e-Ali portfolio — two things. (1) Applied all 5 rows from the find-animation-opportunities report run last turn: .theme-toggle:active + .cs-cta__link:active press-scale (140ms, all 7 case studies), .stat/.edu-block/.award-item added to nav.js's reveal-pending scroll-reveal selector list, and arrow-nudge-on-hover (translateX(2px), 150ms) extended to .proj__link/.project-featured__link/.project-supporting__detail to match the nav CTA arrow added earlier. (2) User sent mobile screenshots calling the nav 'not professional grade' -- spotted a real bug in the menu-open screenshot: .nav-brand__name ('Sibt-e-Ali') was wrapping to two lines ('Sibt-e-\nAli') only when the mobile menu was open. Root cause: .nav-toggle rendered literal text 'Menu'/'Close' via nav.js's toggle.textContent, and 'Close' (5 chars) is wider than 'Menu' (4 chars) -- enough to squeeze the flex row and force the wordmark to wrap at narrow widths. Fixed by converting .nav-toggle to a fixed-size (2rem circle, matching .theme-toggle) icon button -- two .nav-toggle__bar spans that morph hamburger to X via transform:rotate(), constant footprint regardless of state. nav.js no longer touches textContent, only aria-label/aria-expanded. Added white-space:nowrap to .nav-brand__name as a second line of defense. Also tightened the mobile nav-menu dropdown's link spacing (480px override was forcing gap:var(--space-lg)/32px, looked loose/unpolished in the screenshot; removed the override so it falls back to the tighter base gap). Batch-applied the nav-toggle markup change across all 13 pages via Python regex (3 different HTML formatting variants across files), verified via grep (nav-toggle__bar: 13/13, zero leftover '>Menu</button>').
scope: index.css, projects.css, nav.js, all 13 HTML pages (nav-toggle markup only), 7 case-study <style> blocks (cs-cta__link), design.md

Redesigned index.css nav rules: .site-header is now an inset floating pill (position:sticky, margin-inline, --color-card/--radius-pill/--shadow-card) instead of a full-bleed hairline strip -- fixing the exact N1 anti-pattern hallmark's own anti-patterns.md names. Wordmark became a two-line brand lockup (.nav-brand__mark 'SB' initials tile + .nav-brand__name + .nav-brand__role 'Software Engineer', reused verbatim from the hero label rather than invented) -- checked for a real headshot photo first (found only a blank/transparent placeholder PNG, 879x126, unusable) so used an initials mark instead of fabricating an avatar. Nav links get a soft pill hover/active background instead of a bare colour change; CTA gained a '->' that nudges right on hover. Non-trivial part: .site-nav becomes display:contents at desktop (a pre-existing trick that merges .site-nav and the sibling .nav-menu into one flex row on .site-header) -- pill background can't live on an element that stops generating a box, so the visual chrome had to move to .site-header inside the desktop media query specifically, while staying on .site-nav for the mobile-collapsed state where .site-nav is still a real box. Also gave the mobile dropdown .nav-menu its own card surface (it used to just inherit .site-header's old flat background, which no longer exists). Batch-edited the HTML wordmark + CTA markup identically across all 13 pages (4 root + 9 project pages) via a Python regex pass, verified with grep counts (nav-brand: 13/13, nav-cta__arrow: 13/13, zero leftover .nav-name).
